clocks.label: SALALAH TALKS
clocks.why: Gulf foreign ministers meet Iran's in Oman to seek buy-in for a temporary arrangement to manage Hormuz shipping. This clock prices GEO-013 at 76 per cent - whether any deal preserves Iranian transit-administration machinery - and it is the first scheduled test that question has had.

clocks.label: FOMC DECISION
clocks.why: The meeting behind GEO-029, raised to 72 per cent today on an August CPI of 3.4 per cent with core accelerating to 0.3 per cent on the month. Watch the statement's sentence about energy rather than the rate - the ECB dropped look-through last week and the language is where the decision actually lives.

clocks.label: BOJ DECISION
clocks.why: The confirmation leg for GEO-025 at 31 per cent. USD/JPY has run from 160.20 to 153.42 in about seven sessions and the barrier is 147.20; a hike is the Tokyo half of the 2024 carry-unwind template. The published falsifier is a hold that sends the yen back through 158.

clocks.label: HORMUZ FALSIFIER
clocks.why: A falsifier this ledger published in advance on its escalation model. If the named Hormuz-zone event has not occurred by this date, non-occurrence is scored AGAINST the model rather than rolled forward - which is the only way a forecast book stays honest.

clocks.label: XI IN WASHINGTON
clocks.why: GEO-006 at 92 per cent, and today's Delhi appearance is logistics evidence for it. It also starts the clock on GEO-012, which asks whether a concrete Hormuz concession follows within thirty days of a concluded summit.

clocks.label: RUSSIA DIESEL BAN
clocks.why: Moscow's export ban carries a published expiry and it is the only one of the forces holding the diesel crack at a record that has a date attached. GEO-026 at 24 per cent needs either crude to fall or conversion capacity to return; this is the nearest scheduled chance of the latter.

speculation.obs: A named research institute put an instrument on the Saudi pipeline claim and the claim got smaller. Mikhail Zhizhin and Morgan Bazilian of the Payne Institute at the Colorado School of Mines, using VIIRS Nightfire data from the Suomi NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 satellites cross-read against NASA FIRMS and Sentinel-3, found that on 10-11 September at least two KNOWN flares along the East-West pipeline entered an apparent 'emergency' operating regime, with flow rates jumping abruptly to roughly 0.32-0.44 billion cubic metres a year at combustion temperatures within each site's previously observed range - one flare, catalogued as s_8831 at 23.95909N 40.05338E, sitting near the reported fire. They state the observations 'do not indicate new fires at unusual or previously uncatalogued locations'.
speculation.src: Payne Institute for Public Policy, Colorado School of Mines (VIIRS Nightfire, NASA FIRMS, Sentinel-3)
speculation.read: Labelled inference, and it runs against the loud version of the story rather than with it - which is exactly why it is worth logging. Emergency flaring at flares that already existed is the signature of a line being depressurised in a hurry: a shut-in, a valve isolation, an upstream halt. It is not the signature of eight new rupture points, which would light up coordinates with no catalogue entry. So the physical evidence supports 'something forced an unplanned stoppage on this system' and specifically fails to support the diplomatic claim of catastrophic multi-point damage. Hold both halves. A pipeline that has been emergency-depressurised is not a pipeline that is pumping.
speculation.falsifier: Nightfire or FIRMS detections at uncatalogued coordinates along the Abqaiq-Yanbu route would confirm actual ruptures and kill the shut-in reading. Flares returning to baseline flow within days, with no Aramco force majeure, would say the interruption was brief and local.

speculation.obs: The transit trackers show the strait thinning in steps rather than closing, and the Saudi traffic going the other way round the map. Lloyd's List Intelligence recorded 302 passages through Bab al-Mandab in the week of 17-23 August, of which 257 were AIS-traceable, then 202 traceable transits over 24-30 August - against an average of 273 ships a week between 27 July and 23 August and a pre-ban weekly average of 319 before Saudi Arabia's naval ban took effect on 20 July. The same brief attributes part of the Suez Canal's recovery to 'rerouting of Saudi traffic northbound', noting that Yanbu cargoes which previously transited the Red Sea are increasingly routed north via Suez.
speculation.src: Lloyd's List Intelligence Red Sea Brief, 3 September 2026
speculation.read: Labelled inference. Two things sit in this data that the headlines keep merging. First, the lane is repricing rather than closing - a fall from 319 to the low 200s is an insurance and routing story, the equilibrium a toll-taker wants, not the one that brings warships. Second, and newer: the Saudi-specific carve-out announced today was already visible in the routing weeks before anyone announced it, because Yanbu barrels going NORTH through Suez means the southern exit was functionally shut to Saudi cargo back in August. That reorders the causation - today's declaration ratified a fact rather than creating one. Carried openly: public transit series lag and revise, and the AIS-traceable subset understates traffic because ships in contested water go dark.
speculation.falsifier: A weekly traceable count falling below roughly 150 would mean closure rather than repricing. A recovery toward 319, or Yanbu cargoes reappearing southbound, would say the carve-out is being ignored and the toll is not binding.

speculation.obs: Specialist imagery accounts documented the airstrips on the Bab al-Mandab islands long before anyone was fighting for them. As reported by The War Zone using Planet Labs imagery, Perim (Mayyun) carries a runway of roughly 6,150 feet built by the UAE in 2021 and Zuqar a strip of about 2.1km built in 2025; the accounts OSINTtechnical, Open Source Intel and AfriMEOSINT separately documented Ansar Allah forces at Mokha airport and captured equipment this week. TWZ said it could not independently confirm the reported capture of either island.
speculation.src: Planet Labs imagery and named OSINT accounts, compiled by The War Zone
speculation.read: Labelled inference, retained because its falsifier is now the single most load-bearing observable on the board. A 6,150-foot runway on a volcanic rock less than two miles off the Yemeni coast is not local infrastructure - it is a platform, built by one belligerent during its own intervention and inherited by another. Today's argument is about whether Ansar Allah 'holds' Perim; the question that decides whether the strait is priced or closed is whether anything gets emplaced on that strip. Note what has NOT been observed after a full day of claimed control: no imagery of radar, missiles or aircraft on either runway.
speculation.falsifier: Imagery showing aircraft, radar or air defence on the Perim or Zuqar strips confirms the platform reading. Continued absence of any airframe or emitter through end-September makes the runways a legacy artefact and the capture a symbolic one.

dossiers.name: Iran

glance.government: Islamic Republic - a clerical-military hybrid in which the security institutions have been ascendant since the February-May war
glance.leader: Mojtaba Khamenei, Supreme Leader since 8 Mar 2026, not verifiably seen in public for roughly six months; Masoud Pezeshkian president; IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi the operative center
glance.gdp: Roughly $300-390bn nominal depending on source; forecast to contract about 5% in 2026 with inflation near 70% and the rial at a record 2.02m to the dollar
glance.military: About 570,000-610,000 active (IISS puts it near 570,000) plus roughly 350,000 reserves; the IRGC Navy, not the regular navy, holds the strait
glance.influence: Transit rights and mine inventory at Hormuz, anti-ship missiles, Iraqi and Yemeni networks - set against oil revenue the central bank governor himself describes as having fallen to zero

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint, not the man. Iran is a state whose one convertible asset - the barrel - has stopped moving, which is why its remaining leverage is geographic rather than economic, and why it is spent in advertised doses rather than banked. The desk that decides is the IRGC Navy and the new wartime security committee, not the presidency and not the invisible Leader: Washington routed its own peace offer through career Guard commanders, and Iran's president has said on state television that communicating with Khamenei is very difficult. That produces exactly the behaviour this board keeps recording - a volley at forewarned bases in Jordan that was almost entirely intercepted, mines laid and lanes conditionally cleared, six near-breakthroughs that each end in a restated condition. Prospect theory says a cornered regime gambles, but a regime whose survival runs through an institution that profits from the crisis has an interest in holding the temperature where it can still choose it. The falsifier is a strike that actually kills Americans, or a verified minesweeping calendar with published coordinates - either would show the temperature is no longer being chosen.

concerns: Mine and anti-ship capability at Hormuz is intact and reversible - a cleared lane is a maintenance schedule, not a settlement
Succession is unresolved in practice: an unseen Leader plus an IRGC that answers Washington's messages is a leadership fiction with a real chain of command underneath
Oil revenue near zero against 70% inflation removes the economic off-ramp that would normally price restraint
Escalation is now probabilistic rather than intentional - interception rates, not decisions, separate a message from a casualty event

Retaliation has gone HORIZONTAL: fire into US facilities in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait in a single night widens the number of surfaces on which the interception equilibrium can fail, and converts Gulf hosts from venues into potential parties

The war has reached the LOADING POINT: Iranian state media says four US missiles hit a tanker six miles off Kharg on 5 September, and Iran fired anti-ship and ballistic missiles toward the strait the day before. Unconfirmed, and the terminals themselves are still unstruck - but the one asset with any convertible value left is now inside the target set

A SECOND CHOKEPOINT, bought without an Iranian casualty: with Ansar Allah holding the Yemeni bank of Bab el-Mandeb, Tehran now has a hand on two of the six places where seaborne trade passes single file. Note what that does to the bargaining table rather than the battlefield - a Red Sea chip is SEPARABLE, tradeable away without Iran conceding anything of its own, which makes a Hormuz settlement cheaper for Tehran and not more expensive. The principal-agent risk runs the other way: Ansar Allah has its own war aims at Taiz and its own scores with Riyadh, and a proxy that acquires territory acquires independence

dossiers.name: Saudi Arabia

glance.government: Absolute monarchy; day-to-day rule exercised by Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman on behalf of King Salman
glance.leader: Mohammed bin Salman, Crown Prince and PM; the decisive desks are the Royal Court, the Ministry of Defence under Khalid bin Salman, and Aramco
glance.gdp: Roughly $1.1tn nominal; fiscal breakeven oil price is materially above the pre-war Brent strip, which is why a high barrel is not simply good news for Riyadh
glance.military: About 250,000 active across services plus the SANG; heavily equipped and air-dominant, with a demonstrated shortage of deployable INFANTRY - the constraint that just cost it Mocha
glance.influence: Spare crude capacity, Ras Tanura and Yanbu as the world's principal loading complex, and since the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement a publicly stated Pakistani security commitment

dossiers.summary: Start with the constraint. Riyadh's problem is not resolve, it is force structure: it can generate air strikes in a day and cannot generate a brigade that will hold a coastline, which is why its Yemeni position is a patchwork of rival Saudi- and Emirati-funded militias that has now lost Mocha, Dhubab and the island of Perim in a single week. Today the second constraint became visible and it is the more consequential one. The kingdom's eastern outlet has been shut by the Hormuz permit regime since the war; its western outlet runs past a strait whose eastern bank is now held by Ansar Allah; and satellites show a fire burning along the route of the East-West pipeline that feeds Yanbu, the one export path that avoids Hormuz altogether - unconfirmed, with Aramco silent. On OPEC's own numbers August production fell to its lowest since 1990. The desk that decides is the Royal Court plus Aramco, not the foreign ministry, and Aramco's revealed preference across fifty years is to protect its reliability franchise: after Abqaiq in 2019 it lost about half its output and still declined to declare force majeure, delivering from storage. The third fact of the day is the one that changes the strategic picture rather than the barrel: Mohammed bin Salman asked the American president twice on Thursday for strikes on the Houthis and was refused, receiving intelligence, targeting data and a CENTCOM visit instead. Sagan's security model prices what follows - a client hedges when the credibility of its guarantee falls, not when the threat rises - and the hedging instruments to watch are reactor tenders, enrichment language and further operationalising of the Mecca pact with Pakistan, not a bomb. The falsifier remains a strike on an EXPORT terminal rather than a refinery: that is the rung at which Riyadh stops taxing its own margins and starts losing its only convertible asset.

concerns: Both westward outlets are under pressure at once - Bab el-Mandeb's eastern bank is held by Ansar Allah and a fire burns over the Petroline route, while Hormuz remains shut by permit
No deployable ground force in Yemen - coalition units withdrew from Mocha and from Perim rather than hold them, and air power cannot retake a coast
The American guarantee has been publicly tested and found partial: freedom of navigation for the lane, intelligence and targeting data for the land war, no strikes
Refining capacity is being taxed repeatedly: Jazan, 400,000 b/d and about a tenth of Aramco's net refining, has been hit or shut three times since late July, and Tuesday's assault injured at least 73
Export infrastructure at Ras Tanura and Yanbu remains untouched - still the single most consequential unfired tripwire on this board
Fiscal breakeven above the strip means a war premium does not pay for itself; the kingdom needs volume as much as price, and volume is what both a terminal strike and a pipeline outage would take

dossiers.name: Russia

glance.government: Presidential autocracy with a managed legislature; State Duma elections due September 2026
glance.leader: Vladimir Putin - the only decider on the war file; Peskov is a thermostat, not an actor
glance.population: About 144 million (2026 estimate; occupied-territory counting disputed)
glance.gdp: Roughly $2.7tn nominal; the government cut its 2026 growth forecast toward 0.4-1%, with oil and gas revenue reported down more than 25%
glance.military: About 1.3 million active with roughly 2 million reserves; defence spending near 6.3-6.5% of GDP
glance.influence: Sanctioned-barrel logistics including the Arctic route, Africa Corps guarantees in the Sahel, energy leverage over Europe, veto and nuclear status

dossiers.summary: Moscow's constraint is refining and money, not morale. Ukrainian deep strikes have pushed refinery runs to about 3.6m barrels a day, the lowest since 2002, and the fuel export ban first imposed in July is being weighed for a second extension - each extension a public admission of how much capacity is offline. The deciding desks are the defence and finance ministries rather than the foreign ministry: the September Duma election and the 6.3-6.5% of GDP the war costs are what price the negotiating posture, which is why the deep pause Peskov announced reads as a bargaining position taken from a front that is still moving at Pokrovsk. Watch where the state chose to spend a scarce asset this weekend - Africa Corps, roughly 200-300 personnel supplied overland through Burkina Faso, was used to save a junta in Niamey, buying an advertisement and incurring an obligation in the same act. The observables that would move this file are not statements but airlift and diesel: Flight Unit 224 traffic above its six-flight run rate, or refinery runs recovering past 4m barrels a day.

concerns: The fuel and refining constraint is the real bind - denial is working where punishment has not, and Kyiv is aiming at exactly that
The announced campaign against Ukraine's grid is punishment by Pape's definition, with a poor historical conversion into concessions
Sahel guarantees now carry a defend-the-palace obligation a 200-300 person detachment cannot scale
September Duma elections and a possible post-election reserve call-up are the domestic clock every diplomatic signal is priced against

The covert front against the supplier coalition is now formally attributed: Berlin blames Moscow for an explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle and closes the Bonn consulate on Sept 18, with the EU calling it state-sponsored terrorism - salami tactics against logistics rather than against forces

First reciprocated pause of the war, and it is a bargaining instrument rather than fatigue: Putin ordered no strikes on Kyiv for 72 hours from midnight on 5 September, explicitly tied to the American envoys' visit, hours after striking Ukrainian airports and infrastructure and with Ryabkov restating that Washington must accept realities on the ground

dossiers.name: Ukraine

glance.government: Wartime presidential republic under martial law; national elections suspended for the duration
glance.leader: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, constrained by coalition dependence; Rustem Umerov holds both the negotiating brief and the intelligence file
glance.population: About 39.5 million on mid-2026 estimates - wartime displacement makes every figure soft
glance.gdp: Roughly $225bn nominal (2025); the EU agreed a package of about EUR 90bn for 2026-27, funded by market borrowing rather than by seizing the roughly EUR 210bn of frozen Russian assets
glance.military: About 677,000 active on the IISS count; larger figures circulate and are not verified
glance.influence: A deep-strike drone campaign that has taken Russian refining to a 24-year low, the Black Sea corridor, and the political weight of being the coalition's test case

dossiers.summary: Kyiv's constraint is arithmetic - manpower, interceptors and a donor calendar - and it sets the strategy rather than following from it. The one instrument Ukraine owns outright is the drone campaign against Russian refineries, which is denial in Pape's sense and is measurably working; nearly everything else is rented from capitals that vote. That dependence is why the deciding desk is now split between the general staff and a negotiating channel run through Washington, and why Zelenskyy has to say yes to the joint Western plan and no to surrender in the same breath. It also explains Myla: an army under sustained deep strike disperses munitions into settlements, which lowers the odds of losing a depot and raises the odds of a night like Friday's, when 38 people died mostly from what the warehouse contained. The falsifiable claim for the winter is that Russia's fuel constraint shapes Russian behaviour more than blackouts shape Ukrainian negotiating positions - if Kyiv's position visibly softens under grid attack while Moscow's does not under fuel shortage, the model is wrong and we say so.

concerns: The announced Russian campaign against the electricity grid arrives with winter and with air-defence stocks already rationed
Pokrovsk is the axis Moscow names when it explains why it is in no hurry to talk; its fall would be a step change, not a line move
Funding is market-borrowed rather than asset-backed, which puts the money on a European political calendar
Dispersal of munitions into inhabited areas makes mass-casualty events recurrent regardless of anyone's aimpoint

dossiers.name: China

glance.government: Party-state under the most centralized leadership since Mao; a recent command purge reshaped the military timetable
glance.leader: Xi Jinping; Wang Yi carries the foreign file with delegated authority
glance.gdp: About $20.9tn nominal (IMF, 2026); 4.7% growth in the first half against a 4.5-5% target, July exports up 23.9% year on year
glance.military: About 2.0 million active, the largest standing force in the world; announced defence budget in the $280bn range
glance.influence: Buyer of last resort for sanctioned barrels, rare earths and the export machine, coast-guard jurisdiction pressure around Taiwan and the East China Sea, and a summit Washington wants

dossiers.summary: Beijing's constraint this quarter is the calendar, not the doctrine. A state visit on 24 September and a tariff truce expiring in November are both worth more than any concession on Iranian crude, which is why the buying continues while the rhetoric stays defiant - and why Treasury sanctioned an Egyptian bank's UAE branches rather than a Chinese one. An enforcer that keeps picking the cheapest nail is telling you which nail is expensive. The desk to watch is not the foreign ministry but the coast guard and the customs administration: PLA sorties around Taiwan have been declining while jurisdictional assertion has been rising, and that ratchet - salami tactics in Schelling's sense, slices too thin to fight over individually - is the actual instrument. Read the summit as accumulation under cover of detente rather than as a thaw, and keep the discount small: announced head-of-state visits with active staff preparation happen about 90% of the time. The tell that breaks the benign read is a coast-guard action inside the visit window; the tell that breaks the leverage read is a blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank before 24 September.

concerns: Coast-guard normalization and seabed mapping are precondition-building around Taiwan, not the event itself
China is the load-bearing leak in the Iran sanctions siege - Mulder's rule is that a siege is only as tight as its leakage path
The tariff truce expires in November, just after the summit, which is where a cheap concession becomes an expensive one
A defiant public line paired with quiet compliance makes intent unreadable from statements; only flows settle it

dossiers.name: Israel

glance.government: Parliamentary democracy; the Knesset dissolved in July and the election is set for 27 October 2026
glance.leader: Benjamin Netanyahu, prime minister; Israel Katz defence minister and the cabinet's designated hawk
glance.gdp: About $720bn nominal on 2026 estimates, with defence spending near 8% of GDP
glance.influence: Air superiority over the Levant, the Washington relationship, and an undeclared nuclear status the state has never confirmed

dossiers.summary: Read every Israeli decision for the next seven weeks through 27 October. That is the constraint, and it is a calendar rather than a character: a prime minister facing an election needs deliverables that are visible, mapped and finished, which is exactly what a declared security zone is. On 4 September Katz said the capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge completes the phase of securing control in southern Lebanon and that there will be no withdrawal until Hezbollah is disarmed throughout the country - a condition the Lebanese state has never been able to meet, which makes the presence open-ended by construction. The desk that decides is not the cabinet podium but Northern Command's force-generation math and the finance ministry's reserve-duty bill, because holding ground costs manpower in a way air power does not. Note also the direction this cuts: history says a held buffer produces chronic attrition rather than episodic campaigns, which is why this board CUT its multi-week-campaign odds on the day the zone was declared. Separately, national security minister Ben Gvir published a twenty-page plan for what he calls voluntary emigration of Gaza's population - 250,000 in the first year and the remainder over six more. It is a minister's document rather than cabinet policy, and forced transfer of civilians from occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; it is logged here as a coalition signal, not as a programme.

concerns: The 27 October election makes restraint politically expensive at exactly the wrong moment
A withdrawal condition the Lebanese state cannot satisfy converts an operation into an occupation by definition
The Lebanon framework still has no third-party verifier and the party being disarmed rejects the premise
Ministerial transfer plans for Gaza, even unimplemented, carry legal and coalition exposure that outlasts the cabinet

dossiers.name: Germany

glance.government: Federal parliamentary republic; sixteen Laender, each electing its own Minister-President. Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote 20 September 2026
glance.leader: Friedrich Merz, chancellor, whose CDU just lost 25 of its 40 seats in Saxony-Anhalt; Ulrich Siegmund leads the AfD there and has said he will not stand for Minister-President without a stable majority
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.9tn nominal - unverified against a current print; Jaguar Land Rover cutting 4,000 jobs and Volkswagen repurposing a plant for defence are the texture of the industrial quarter
glance.military: About 182,000 active on standard counts, with rearmament running against recruitment shortfalls; unverified against a current IISS figure
glance.influence: Europe's largest industrial gas consumer, the logistics bridge to Ukraine through Leipzig/Halle, and the swing vote on every EU sanctions and energy instrument

dossiers.summary: Germany's constraint stopped being abstract on Sunday. The AfD took 43.9 per cent and 39 of 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt on turnout that rose from about 60 to about 80 per cent, and the CDU fell to 17.2 per cent - which means the late-mobilisation argument that has contained the AfD in every previous Land election did not work, and ING said so in as many words. The desk that now decides is not the federal party presidium in Berlin, which can only expel people; it is the Landtag running ballots in Magdeburg, where a third round for Minister-President is settled by a simple majority of votes cast and the five-seat BSW can decide the outcome by abstaining. Underneath the politics the older vice is unchanged: Germany replaced Russian pipeline gas with seaborne LNG, trading a political dependency for a maritime one, so a war at Hormuz reaches German industry directly - and it remains the physical bridge over which munitions reach Ukraine, which is why a drone came down at Leipzig/Halle rather than at a barracks. Two more elections land on 20 September.

concerns: A Land where no majority exists without breaking one of two taboos - the CDU has excluded both the AfD and Die Linke, and the third-ballot rule rewards deadlock
Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern vote on 20 September, thirteen days after the mobilisation defence visibly failed
Fraud narratives spread within hours of the count, part of them traced by DW's fact-check desk to the Matryoshka influence operation - contested results are now a standing feature of German elections
A sabotage campaign aimed at logistics rather than forces sits deliberately below any alliance threshold, and Lavrov has answered Berlin's attribution by calling it the start of a real war
Energy input cost remains the binding industrial number, and seaborne LNG means Hormuz is now a German domestic-politics variable

dossiers.name: United States

glance.government: Federal presidential republic; midterm elections 3 November 2026
glance.leader: Donald Trump; Scott Bessent at Treasury, Marco Rubio at State, Pete Hegseth at Defense, Kevin Warsh at the Federal Reserve
glance.gdp: Roughly $30tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; federal debt past $40tn
glance.military: About 1.34 million active with roughly 770,000 reserve and National Guard; budget in the $900bn range
glance.influence: Dollar clearing and OFAC designations, CENTCOM escort of the strait, and a rate path that prices everyone else's oil bill

dossiers.summary: The American constraint hardened today and it is arithmetic rather than politics. August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus with unemployment at 4.1%, which removes the soft-landing argument for cutting; simultaneously diesel set an all-time record at $5.820 a gallon on a refining shortage no interest rate can fix. That is the RESCUE WITHHELD configuration - a market pricing help in a shock where help does not exist - and the long end already agrees, with the ten-year at 4.79% and the thirty-year at 5.27%, both above this board's published red lines, and the reverse-repo buffer down to $0.70bn. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the FOMC, the refiners' turnaround calendar and the weekly EIA distillate print, in that order of who can actually change the number. Foreign policy is being run on the same logic - allies invoiced for contributions at Hormuz, a Venezuelan venture organised around one man's legal exposure rather than around built infrastructure, and a president who declined this week to say whether the United States would defend Britain in another Falklands war. Each of those is leverage bought cheaply now against a commitment payable later.

concerns: Record diesel is the invisible half of the inflation problem, because it prices freight, farming and heating rather than only the pump
A hot labour print into a hiking debate removes the monetary rescue markets keep assuming
Enforcement at Hormuz is now a standing commitment - a lane you must keep clearing is not a victory
Alliance ambiguity is being used as leverage in three theatres at once, and credibility spent in one is not recoverable in another
Confirmed American casualties would collapse the intercepted-volley equilibrium the whole restraint posture rests on

dossiers.name: Japan

glance.government: Constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system; Bank of Japan policy decision due 18 September 2026
glance.leader: Emperor Naruhito as head of state; the offices that matter for this file are the Bank of Japan policy board and the Ministry of Finance FX desk - not the cabinet
glance.gdp: Roughly $4.2tn nominal on standard 2026 estimates - unverified against a current print; policy rate 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, with ten-year government bond yields near 3 per cent for the first time since 1996
glance.military: Self-Defense Forces of about 247,000 active personnel; defence spending on a path toward 2 per cent of GDP
glance.influence: The world's cheap funding currency, one of the largest foreign holders of US Treasuries, and a carry trade estimated anywhere between $500bn and over $4tn depending on definition

dossiers.summary: Japan's constraint became visible in a number this week: 15.4 trillion yen, about $98.6bn, spent in a single month defending the currency, and reporting that it likely sold US Treasuries to fund it. For thirty years Japan supplied the world with money that cost nothing and the world spent it on everything from Mexican bonds to American technology; that arrangement is unwinding because Japan finally has inflation, imported partly through a weak yen and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption made worse. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board on 18 September, and the yen has already run to 154.06 on the expectation. What is genuinely new is the American side of the plumbing: Washington joined the July intervention and Bessent pushed the Fed to widen the FIMA repo facility, which lets Tokyo borrow dollars against its Treasuries instead of selling them. Read that as the balance-of-financial-terror being actively managed - the US needs its largest foreign creditor not to become a seller during a heavy issuance calendar, and it built a valve to make sure.

concerns: A disorderly carry unwind transmits a Tokyo rate decision into global asset prices within hours, as it did in August 2024
The size of the borrowed-yen stack is genuinely unknown - published estimates span an order of magnitude
A currency defence funded by Treasury sales raises US long-end yields at the exact moment the ten-year sits above 4.75 per cent
A defence financed by repo must be repeatedly refinanced, which converts a one-off intervention into a standing obligation
Imported energy costs are the transmission line from the Strait of Hormuz into Japanese inflation and therefore into this policy decision

scenarios.q: What if the Petroline pipeline is confirmed damaged?
scenarios.read: This is the single branch on the board where a physical fact, not a policy, sets the price. The East-West line is Saudi Arabia's only export route that avoids Hormuz, and the kingdom is already exporting into a Red Sea whose southern gate is now held by a hostile force. The mechanism is not 'less oil exists' - it is that barrels which cannot reach water stop being supply. Note the base rate cuts against catastrophe: Aramco restored this same line quickly after a 2019 drone strike, and after Abqaiq it protected its reliability franchise by delivering from storage rather than declaring force majeure.

stages.s: A - Aramco stays silent, loading programmes run normally through October, and the plume is attributed to a non-pipeline fire; the premium decays within two weeks
B - a repairable impairment is acknowledged or inferred from throughput data, Aramco draws on storage, and the market prices weeks rather than quarters
C - a confirmed throughput reduction or a force majeure at Yanbu; both Saudi outlets are impaired at once and the Brent barrier question re-rates sharply upward
D - repeated strikes make the route structurally unreliable and Gulf exports become a storage-and-rationing problem rather than a routing one

scenarios.falsifier: Published Yanbu loading programmes running normally through October kills stages C and D outright and scores the 40 per cent opening on GEO-032 as too hot.

scenarios.q: What if Bab el-Mandeb is priced shut rather than fought shut?
scenarios.read: Closure by quotation is how narrow seas have actually been closed for four centuries - not by sinking ships but by an underwriting committee moving a line on a chart. The carve-out doing the work right now is that war-risk quotations still distinguish Saudi-linked tonnage, at up to 3 per cent of hull value, from general trade at roughly 0.5 per cent. Ansar Allah's spokesman insists navigation is safe and uninterrupted, which is exactly what a party that wants a toll rather than a blockade would say. The western littoral is Djibouti and Eritrea, so this is contestation, not sovereignty.

stages.s: A - the carve-out holds, non-Saudi traffic keeps sailing at a higher premium, and the strait becomes expensive rather than closed
B - quotations stop distinguishing Saudi-linked tonnage; general transits fall sharply and Cape reroutes become the default for Gulf-Europe distillate
C - anti-ship systems are verifiably emplaced on Perim and the lane closes in practice for laden tankers; Suez revenue collapses as a second-order effect
D - a multinational escort or amphibious operation to retake the island, which the American posture as stated today argues against

scenarios.falsifier: A Lloyd's weekly transit count holding near the 273-a-week pre-Mocha baseline through October would say the strait was repriced and absorbed, killing stages C and D.

scenarios.q: What if the Fed tightens into the oil shock on 16 September?
scenarios.read: The trap is that an interest rate is a demand instrument and cannot produce a barrel of diesel. Today's release hands the committee both arguments in one document: core accelerated to 0.3 per cent on the month, and core on the YEAR fell to 2.4 per cent from 2.5. Three members dissented for a hike in July and the ECB abandoned look-through last week, which raises the reputational cost of the Fed doing the opposite. Watch the language before the number - the statement's sentence about energy is the decision.

stages.s: A - hikes on 16 September; the dollar firms into an oil shock, which is the oil-up-and-dollar-up tape the plumbing lens treats as diagnostic
B - holds but DROPS the pass-through language, signalling a November move; the long end steepens further
C - holds with look-through language intact and the dissent bloc unchanged; the question survives to November and December on three-meeting optionality
D - cuts or signals easing on growth fears; the rescue arrives and the rescue-withheld read is falsified

scenarios.falsifier: A cut, or an explicit easing signal, at either the September or November meeting kills this branch outright and scores the desk's hawkish lean as wrong.

chatter.claim: That pre-attack insider trading is the key that unlocks 9/11 - that put options on the airlines, and the career of a former Marsh & McLennan employee at the World Trade Center, show the operation was run above the level of any single state, described in the thread as 'Rothschild-tier' rather than the work of any one government.
chatter.spread: A 193-reply /pol/ thread built around a Rumble interview, one of the highest-traffic anniversary threads on the board
chatter.read: The above-the-state frame, and it is the anniversary's most durable specimen because it has a checkable kernel. The options activity was real and was investigated specifically; the 9/11 Commission traced the largest positions to institutional hedging. People are entitled to distrust that finding, but the frame does not engage it - it treats the existence of the trades as the conclusion. Note the structure: moving the culprit above every state makes the claim unfalsifiable by any government's records.

chatter.claim: An ethnic-scapegoat narrative is circulating at high volume around the 9/11 anniversary, asserting that a named religious group planned and executed the attacks, citing the existence of an FBI file on five men detained in 2001 and a trademark filing made shortly after the first impact as proof.
chatter.spread: A run of /pol/ threads through the day, several cross-posted into the anniversary generals, plus counter-threads objecting to them
chatter.read: The content is not repeated here. The persuasion technique is the one worth naming: cite a real document, then treat the document's EXISTENCE as confirmation of what it does not say - an investigative file records that something was investigated, which is the opposite of a finding. The second move is to supply a culprit whose guilt requires no evidence because the audience already believed it. Logged because the traffic is data about belief in 2026, not about 2001.

chatter.claim: That 9/11 was an inside job and the American government knew it was coming and deliberately did nothing - and, in a companion thread, that this is why other governments including US adversaries have stayed silent about it for twenty-five years.
chatter.spread: Multiple /pol/ threads including a 197-reply 'everything the public is told is bullshit' thread and a 134-reply thread complaining the board has 'too many 9/11 defenders'
chatter.read: The let-it-happen-on-purpose frame, the most resilient variant because it needs no demolition physics, only institutional failure, and institutional failure is documented. The kernel is genuine and is exactly what today's CIA release is about: warnings existed, were circulated to two administrations, and were not acted on. The frame converts documented incompetence into intent, a far larger claim requiring evidence nobody has produced. The silence-of-adversaries argument inverts itself on contact - Moscow and Tehran have every incentive to publish proof and have not.

chatter.claim: That jet fuel could not have brought down the towers - a thread running the numbers that structural steel melts around 2,750F while jet fuel burns at 800-1,500F, concluding the official account is thermodynamically impossible.
chatter.spread: A /pol/ anniversary thread, with /x/ running a parallel general on 9/11 predictive programming, occult ties and 'memory-holed' footage
chatter.read: The oldest specimen on the board and the most cleanly answerable: the claim substitutes MELTING for the engineering question, which is loss of yield strength. Structural steel loses roughly half its strength around 1,100F, well inside a hydrocarbon fire's range, and a frame does not need liquid steel to fail - it needs members that can no longer carry load. Logged every anniversary because its persistence is the useful signal: the argument survives not on physics but because 'they said jet fuel melted steel' is a memorable sentence nobody official ever said.

chatter.claim: That Al-Qaeda simply did it - a counter-thread arguing Americans cope endlessly about 9/11 because they cannot accept being beaten by third-world irregulars, and that the conspiracy ecosystem exists to avoid taking the loss.
chatter.spread: A 29-reply /pol/ thread running directly against the board's dominant register, alongside a 42-reply thread cataloguing Madrid, 7/7, Paris, Brussels, Crocus City and 7 October as a single pattern
chatter.read: Logged deliberately, because a monitoring section that only records the fringe reading of a day misrepresents what is actually circulating. This is the psychological-cost frame and it is doing real work in the threads - it reframes conspiracism as face-saving rather than as evidence-weighing, an argument the conspiracist register has no clean answer to. The companion pattern thread then slides from a list of real attacks to a claim about a population, which is the point at which it stops being a list.

chatter.claim: That the fall of Bab al-Mandab means world war is now imminent - that the closure of a second strait feeding directly into Suez drives oil past $500 a barrel and plunges Europe into darkness before winter, and that the United States must now fully engage Iran and its proxies.
chatter.spread: A 97-reply all-caps /pol/ thread, echoed through the 264-reply Persia-Israel general carrying the territorial claims as headline items
chatter.read: The cascade frame. The kernel is real and large - Ansar Allah genuinely took Dhubab, the Hanish group, Zuqar and Perim inside twenty-four hours - but the price mechanism in the thread is the standard error of this cycle: it converts routing disruption into lost production. Barrels going the long way round are still barrels, which is why the tracked transit count fell to the low 200s rather than to zero, and why Brent traded near $104 rather than near $500.

chatter.claim: That America is a failed state, because the world's largest military cannot stop barefoot irregulars from shutting down oil shipping - with a companion thread asking what hundreds of billions spent on 'revolutionary' AI technology bought, if it cannot beat a light infantry force.
chatter.spread: A 134-reply /pol/ thread and a 93-reply thread on the AI spending comparison, among the highest-traffic non-anniversary items of the day
chatter.read: The decline frame, and it is the exact mirror of the cascade thread above - the same board simultaneously believes the US is about to be dragged into a world war and that it is too feeble to intervene. The kernel is a genuine asymmetry: cheap anti-ship weapons plus a chokepoint impose costs wildly disproportionate to their price, which is a real and well-documented problem. What the frame supplies is the leap from 'expensive force is poorly matched to this problem' to 'the state has failed'.

chatter.claim: That the Houthis took Perim and the coast by generating an AI deepfake of an enemy commander ordering a retreat, described as 'the cheapest landgrab in the entirety of human history'.
chatter.spread: A small, fast-moving /pol/ thread posted within hours of the capture reports
chatter.read: Unverified, and logged as a specimen of a fast-growing category: the deepfake-explains-it frame, which now attaches to any unexplained military collapse the way 'crisis actors' attaches to any unexplained casualty. The kernel it eats is genuine - Yemeni government forces withdrew from Perim and Dhubab BEFORE the fighting rather than during it, which nobody has satisfactorily explained, and a bloodless collapse invites an exotic cause. Worth watching as a category rather than as a claim.

chatter.claim: That the Iran war is being prolonged because American energy producers are the beneficiaries, citing a Brown University real-time tracker finding Americans have paid an extra $102 billion for petrol and diesel since it began, and posting it as a boast on the administration's behalf. Related threads note California becoming the first state to reach $8 diesel.
chatter.spread: Several /pol/ threads built on a WFLA writeup of the Brown tracker, alongside a 107-reply /biz/ thread on the record diesel print
chatter.read: The war-profiteering frame with a sourced number attached, which is what makes it travel. The $102bn estimate is real and consumer cost is producer revenue, so the kernel holds. The inference to intent does not - and the disconfirming fact is on the same page: an administration absorbing record pump prices five weeks before a midterm is paying a cost no designer of the scheme would choose. This desk prices deliberate American slow-walking at 52 per cent for exactly that reason.

chatter.claim: That the Bank of Japan is going to war with the US Treasury - that the Treasury Secretary said he is 'the house' and calls the game, and that BOJ officials plan a big bet to take the house down.
chatter.spread: A 222-reply /pol/ thread built on two viral X posts, cross-read in the /biz/ markets generals where the day's stock general ran to 412 replies
chatter.read: The duel frame, retained because it grew sharply and because its structural kernel is unusually good: a BOJ hiking cycle genuinely does drain the marginal Japanese bid for US Treasuries, so Tokyo's domestic mandate and Washington's funding needs really are in tension this month - the same tension behind today's ten-year pulling back from 5 per cent being reported as a 'reprieve'. What the frame supplies is intent. Central banks respond to their own price indices rather than declaring war on each other.

chatter.claim: That the Epstein files remain the live suppressed story and that official reluctance to discuss them is itself the evidence - threads noting that the released tranches were redacted so poorly the redactions could be undone, that nothing followed, and that the boards themselves have now lost interest, which posters read as managed rather than natural.
chatter.spread: A 28-reply /pol/ thread on the subject's political sensitivity, a thread on FBI vault records, and a resigned meta-thread about the board's own attention span
chatter.read: The managed-decline frame, and the meta-version is the more interesting one: posters are now theorising about the DECAY of their own conspiracy rather than about its content, which is what a narrative looks like when it has run out of new documents. The checkable kernel is real - the vault releases happened and the redaction quality was genuinely poor - and the honest read is that a story stops moving when no new primary material arrives, which is indistinguishable from suppression only if you already assume the material exists.

easy.bottomLine: The fighters who now control Yemen's whole Red Sea coast said something important today: ships are safe to pass - unless they are Saudi. That is not a wall across the sea, it is a bill addressed to one country. Saudi Arabia already cannot use its eastern exit, because the Strait of Hormuz has been shut since the war with Iran, so its oil now has to go the long way round, north through the Suez Canal, which costs more and takes longer. On Monday, Gulf countries will sit down with Iran in Oman to try to agree rules for that other strait.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, not raised, for the eleventh time running. This app only moves to its top level if an American is killed or an American ship with people on board is hit. Neither happened, even on a day full of frightening headlines. Saying that out loud is the point: a scary day is not the same as the thing we said we were watching for, and moving the dial because the news feels bad is how a warning system stops meaning anything.
easy.markets: Oil is still near $104 a barrel, and diesel - the fuel for lorries and trains - set a record above $6 a gallon, which feeds into the price of nearly everything in a shop. American prices were 3.4 per cent higher than a year ago, a bit more than experts expected. One piece of relief: the interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years came back down from 5 per cent, which makes its debt slightly cheaper to carry.
brief: The fighters now holding Yemen's coast said all ships can pass safely except Saudi ones. Picking on one country instead of blocking everybody is clever, because it squeezes Saudi Arabia hard without giving the world's navies a reason to come and fight them.

Gulf countries will meet Iran in Oman on Monday to try to agree temporary rules for ships using the Strait of Hormuz. The catch is that agreeing rules with Iran also means accepting that Iran hands out the permission slips - and arrangements like that tend to stick around.

Twenty-five years after the 9/11 attacks, the CIA published the warnings about al-Qaeda it had given two presidents beforehand. The bigger question is not what came out today but how much of it is blacked out, because that is where the real decision about honesty gets made.

China's leader flies to India this weekend with about 400 officials, his first visit in nearly seven years. That many people means real business is being done - and the main reason India is willing is that American taxes on Indian goods have made being friendly with China worth more than it used to be.

Mexico is rushing to make a tariff deal with the United States before American elections in November. Canada tried standing firm and got hit with new tariffs instead, so Mexico is trying the opposite approach - and part of the price is a new Mexican law to block Chinese companies from buying Mexican firms.
